newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says lira ERM parity realistic.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says lira ERM parity realistic.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on state television the lira's entry into the European exchange rate mechanism at 990 lire to the mark was realistic and reflected the competitiveness of the Italian economy.
"It's a realistic exchange rate which reflects the competitve power of our companies and therefore nothing is being given away to us but nothing is being taken away from our potential," Prodi said.
"The exchange rate we had been hoping for was 1,000 lire. The difference of one percent does not have substantive importance from an economic point of view," Prodi said.

"And above all it was evident that there was an interest among the other countries to keep a very strong lira rate," he added. "At the end of the negotiation I can say that giving away one percent leaves me satisfied."
He said he was "not 100 percent, but 99 percent" satisfied.
